text:
alex: Hey team, customer Alertly ran into intermittent 401s after we rotated their API key this morning via Vault+KMS. They see ~10% of requests fail, others succeed. Hitting /v1/generate from their Lambda behind API Gateway. Logs attached (snippet below).

maya: Can you paste the exact error from the gateway logs? 401s can be a cached auth result or a malformed header.

alex: Gateway log: `{"status":401,"msg":"invalid_api_key","req_id":"r-12ab"}`. Their curl against prod edge: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -v` returns 401 intermittently.

josh: Any chance the Lambda still has the old key in its env? Do they use Parameter Store or env var baked into the function?

alex: They pull secrets at cold start from SSM and we rotated the vault reference that populates SSM via our rotation job. Confirmed SSM value updated ~09:02 UTC. Lambda env not redeployed.

maya: That smells like a connection-persistent worker reusing an in-memory cached header. If the process fetched key once at cold start and keeps it, rotation won't affect warm invocations.

alex: Agreed. Customer says failures appear after a burst of deployments in their app mesh — some invocations go to warm containers with old key, some to newly cold ones with new key. But the weird bit: some warm containers still succeed after several minutes without restart.

sre-oncall: ops-bot created incident INC-20260317-924 in PagerDuty and linked logs. :rotating_light:

ops-bot: automated note: vault-rewrap job completed at 2026-03-17T09:02:04Z, SSM param updated /services/alertly/api_key.

josh: Could be whitespace/newline at end of the secret when written from Vault to SSM — many clients trim but some libs include trailing newline so signature mismatch only on some codepaths. Try comparing raw bytes.

alex: Ran quick check `aws ssm get-parameter --name /services/alertly/api_key --with-decryption | jq -r .Parameter.Value | od -An -t x1` shows `61 62 63 0a` — there's a trailing 0a.

maya: Yep trailing 
. Some of their HTTP client layers do `.strip()` on header, others don't. That explains flakiness.

josh: Repro steps I recommend for support engineer: 1) Confirm SSM raw value bytes. 2) Check Lambda environment loader code for trimming. 3) Instruct customer to restart warm functions (or redeploy) to pick up the trimmed value. 4) Patch rotation pipeline to ensure secrets are written without trailing newline or base64-encoded safely.

alex: Customer patch: removed newline and restarted a couple of containers — immediate drop to 0% 401s. They also asked whether we should invalidate API gateway auth cache.

maya: We have a gateway auth cache TTL=300s for upstream key validation. If old key was rejected, some downstream caches may serve stale allow/deny decisions. Recommend purge cache for that API key or short TTL until rotation completes.

josh: Also double-check Vault -> SSM transform. Our rotation job uses a templated shell that did `echo "$SECRET" > /tmp/out` which introduced newline. I'll open a quick fix to use printf '%s' instead.

alex: Customer also reported a mobile SDK integration that intermittently succeeded. I traced that to an edge CDN node performing request replay to a warm backend and header normalization (it stripped trailing whitespace) — so some paths normalized and others didn't.

sre-oncall: Action items assigned: josh -> vault-rotator script patch, maya -> guidance doc update on lambda secret loaders, alex -> advise customer redeploy + purge gateway cache. Escalate to eng-runtime if we see other rotations introducing newlines.

ingest-bot: note: support ticket #S-598412 updated with remediation steps and customer confirmation.

maya: TL;DR for runbook: 1) When 401s after rotation, check raw secret bytes in source (Vault/SSM). 2) Look for trailing whitespace/newline. 3) Restart warm processes or implement live secret refresh (watcher/notify). 4) Purge gateway/CDN auth cache if auth decision caching in play. 5) Patch rotation writer to avoid adding newlines (use printf or direct API).

alex: Adding quick commands we used:
```
# raw bytes
aws ssm get-parameter --name /services/alertly/api_key --with-decryption | jq -r .Parameter.Value | od -An -t x1
# test call
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $(aws ssm get-parameter --name /services/alertly/api_key --with-decryption | jq -r .Parameter.Value)" https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -I
```

josh: thx. I'll roll the rotator patch and push a canary today. :thumbsup:

alex: Customer confirmed full recovery after restart and rotator fix. Closing loop. :white_check_mark:
